answer: Each agent collects one river sample at a wharf, locks an 85-credit bond, and files a quill-signed log of its source, time, and turbidity. The sample is split, one half sealed for audit, and an auditor re-tests the sealed half against the log; deviation over 3%, a reused quill signature, or one key filing two samples burns the bond. The first filing costs 50, the kth 50+7(k-1), so the 1000th costs 7043 and 1000 fakes cost 3,546,500 plus 85,000 locked. A rented-sample ring fails: each quill signature is tied to one log and one sealed half. An honest agent pays 50 once, then recovers the bond.
